what:
This repository is a personal knowledge base that stores everything as RDF and never overwrites anything. A change becomes an immutable event graph, and is then materialised into the one graph the interface reads. History and state are written in a single transaction, so they can never disagree.

The drawing is a loop because the system is one: the screen posts a change, the change becomes an operation, the operation becomes an event, the event lands in the store — and the read path walks the same ring back, scoping its queries, resolving labels, rendering fragments and swapping them into the page that started it.

Everything above the ring feeds it: importers and scheduled apps produce the same operations a person would. Everything below defines what the data means — ontologies, SHACL shapes and view specs installed at runtime rather than compiled in. Everything to the right happens after the commit returns, so nothing slow can block a save.

The one place the design and the code have drifted apart is the door. The docs say every write goes through a single endpoint; in fact 26 of 28 commit sites call the event store directly, and the concerns wired at that endpoint — webhooks, validation — do not fire for them. Turn on the Bypasses layer to see the three verified shortcuts.
built:
Three containers: an nginx edge on port 4000, a FastAPI backend on 8001, and RDF4J 5.0.1 with a Lucene index. A fourth, Jaeger, collects traces.

Named graphs
urn:sempkm:current              the state everything reads
urn:sempkm:event:{uuid}         one per commit, immutable
urn:sempkm:model:{id}:ontology  installed vocabulary
urn:sempkm:model:{id}:shapes    SHACL — generates the forms
urn:sempkm:model:{id}:views     view specs — generates tables
urn:sempkm:inferred             OWL 2 RL entailments
urn:sempkm:shared:{uuid}        federated, shared with a peer
Three ways to stand
  • Survey — the plot of ground. Shows the ring: one direction writes, the other reads.
  • Layers — the same parts stacked by request depth, surfaces on top, resources at the bottom. Best for seeing how far a call travels.
  • Volatility — Löwy's decomposition. Clients, managers, engines, resource access, resources, with utilities to one side. Best for seeing what reaches past its neighbour.

Drag the angle dial to 90° for a plan view — height collapses and the drawing becomes a floor plan.
